source.title: LongLLaDA: Unlocking Long Context Capabilities in Diffusion LLMs
source.authors: Xiaoran Liu; Yuerong Song; Zhigeng Liu; Zengfeng Huang; Qipeng Guo; Ziwei He; Xipeng Qiu

record.tranche_reason: The study uses NTK-based RoPE context-length extrapolation and its scaling rule to build LongLLaDA, but does not test the claimed loss-versus-parameters, tokens, or compute laws or compute-optimal allocation.
record.gate_note: The study measures perplexity as context length changes and evaluates retrieval and downstream long-context tasks. These are not tests of power-law loss scaling with model size, training tokens, or compute, nor of downstream predictability from scale or pretraining loss. The LongLLaDA and benchmark results are not rows for the claim versions because they concern context-length extrapolation rather than those scaling relations.
record.test_reason: The study's 'scaling laws' are RoPE/NTK context-extrapolation rules (Liu et al., 2023b), which set the rotary-base factor from target context length. It applies them to diffusion LLMs at inference. It does not measure pretraining loss or downstream performance against parameters, tokens, compute or pretraining loss, so no claim version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also conclude that NTK extrapolation and its RoPE scaling law transfer to diffusion LLMs (6× context, to 24k, training-free). They also find diffusion LLMs match autoregressive models on retrieval, lag on aggregation tasks and excel at QA in RULER. 'Scaling laws' here means RoPE extrapolation rules, not loss-versus-scale laws.
record.recipe_differences: The method applies NTK-based RoPE scaling to extend inference context length; it does not fit or test loss power laws over model size, training tokens, or compute.
record.method_sensitivity: Context-extrapolation and retrieval outcomes vary with the NTK scaling factor and diffusion sampling steps.

fits_no_version.finding: Diffusion LLMs (LLaDA) keep stable perplexity beyond the pretrained context, while LLaMA3 perplexity surges beyond 8k.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Bidirectional diffusion LLMs degrade less than autoregressive LLMs under direct RoPE context extrapolation.

fits_no_version.finding: The NTK scaling-factor rule derived for autoregressive RoPE models (λ = 4, 14, 31 for 8k, 16k, 24k) extends LLaDA's retrieval to those lengths. λ = 55 (32k) fails.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The RoPE-based extrapolation scaling rule (Liu et al., 2023b) transfers to diffusion LLMs at inference, up to about 6× context.

record.problems: The perplexity comparison is shown in a figure without tabulated values or reported uncertainty. The experiments do not fit the loss-scaling relations in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: No results bearing on the listed claim versions were reported. Long-context retrieval, LongBench and RULER results, and NTK-scaled LongLLaDA evaluations were omitted because they test context-length extension or task performance, not the claimed scaling relations.

untested.parts: All: no loss-versus-parameters, tokens or compute measurements.
All: no extrapolation from small-run fits.
All: no shape variation at fixed parameter count.
All: diffusion LLMs are studied, but no power-law loss fits over scale are made.
All: downstream benchmarks (LongBench, RULER) are reported only for ~7-8B models; no scale or loss axis.
All: no fitted exponents or compute-optimal split.

record.verdict_notes: The term 'scaling laws' in this paper refers to context-length/rotary-base rules, a name collision with the phenomenon. Gate decision: T4/uses_without_test (arguably T6). The reader's record is sound.

versions.untested_parts: Not tested: loss scaling with parameters, training tokens, or compute.
Not tested: predictions from power-law fits on smaller training runs.
Not tested: compute-optimal parameter and token allocation.
Not tested: effects of architecture shape at fixed parameter count.
Not tested: whether the claimed loss-scaling form transfers to other modalities or training regimes.
Downstream tasks are evaluated, but not for predictability from model scale or pretraining loss.
Not tested: dependence of the claimed loss-scaling exponents or compute-optimal split on fitting choices or setup.
